judgments.yea_description: Voted to pass HB 5004, which sets new state greenhouse gas emission reduction levels, and new emissions and zero-carbon electricity goals for state agencies. It creates a Connecticut Clean Economy Council to advise on climate and clean energy policy and to plan a transition for workers leaving fossil-fuel jobs. The act also adds heat pump projects to school construction grants, sets up a residential heat pump rebate plan, and directs environmentally sustainable state purchasing and open space acquisition. It passed the Connecticut House of Representatives 98-47 and became law.

judgments.yea_description: Voted to pass HB 6913, which bars nursing homes and managed residential communities from discriminating against residents on grounds including race, religion, sex, gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, marital status, age, and national origin. Facilities must post a nondiscrimination notice, have direct-care staff take cultural competency training, and respect residents' physical privacy during care. The health commissioner may take the same disciplinary action existing law allows for other licensing violations. It passed the Connecticut State Senate 26-10 and became law.

judgments.yea_description: Voted to pass HB 7042, which lets a person harmed by a violation, a municipality, or the state sue firearm makers, distributors, and sellers that fail to put reasonable controls over how firearm products are sold and marketed. It also bars those businesses from advertising in ways that promote unlawful sales or use. The act shortens the lookback period for certain Connecticut misdemeanor convictions that disqualify a person from a handgun permit from 20 years to eight, and adds some out-of-state misdemeanors to the disqualifying list. It states that the crime of unlawfully discharging a firearm does not cover discharging one in lawful self-defense. It passed the Connecticut House of Representatives 100-46 and became law.

judgments.yea_description: Voted to pass HB 7066, which requires every public school to designate an administrator to handle contacts with federal immigration authorities, and requires school boards to add procedures for those contacts to their security and safety plans. School staff cannot be disciplined for following those procedures. The same act restricts state and municipal purchase and use of drones made by covered foreign entities such as China or Russia, limits flying drones near critical infrastructure, and lets college athletes be paid through endorsement contracts and revenue-sharing agreements. The governor later vetoed the act's three appropriations sections. It passed the Connecticut House of Representatives 94-49 and became law.

judgments.yea_description: Voted to pass SB 1, which creates an early childhood education endowment and a health insurance subsidy program for early care staff. It adds special education grant funding, a competitive grant for in-district programs, and a behavioral health support services grant program. The act also creates an educational ombudsperson's office, requires a special education family guide and a model transportation contract, and orders a study of the over-identification of minority students for special education. It passed the Connecticut House of Representatives 101-45 and became law.

judgments.yea_description: Voted to pass SB 3, which requires businesses to advertise goods and services at a price that includes every mandatory fee, leaving out taxes and government-imposed fees. Landlords must likewise include recurring fees in advertised rents. The act creates a right to repair by requiring certain electronics and appliance makers to supply repair manuals, parts, and tools on fair and reasonable terms. It also widens the price gouging law during declared emergencies, and requires annual reminders and easy cancellation for subscriptions that renew automatically. It passed the Connecticut House of Representatives 112-34 and became law.

judgments.yea_description: Voted to pass SB 9, which requires home insurers and mortgage lenders to tell customers about flood risk and flood insurance, and adds flood questions to the residential property condition report. It makes all new single-family home construction subject to coastal site plan review. Municipal evacuation and hazard mitigation plans must address threats from sea level change starting in October 2027, and towns must report data on their culverts and bridges. The act also restricts second-generation anticoagulant rodenticides and neonicotinoid pesticides. It passed the Connecticut House of Representatives 115-33 and became law.

judgments.yea_description: Voted to pass SB 1234, which bars publicly funded libraries from signing or renewing electronic book and digital audiobook agreements that stop the library from performing normal lending and operational functions. The ban only starts 60 days after the secretary of the state determines that other states with at least seven million people combined have passed a substantially similar law. It passed the Connecticut House of Representatives 106-38 and became law.

judgments.yea_description: Voted to pass SB 1328, which bars private ownership, operation, or management of state correctional facilities, community correctional centers, and community reintegration centers. It gives the Department of Correction commissioner and department employees the sole duty of holding and supervising people detained in them. Federally owned or operated facilities are exempt, as are community-based programs offering housing, transportation, employment, and counseling services. It passed the Connecticut House of Representatives 109-37 and became law.

judgments.yea_description: Voted to pass SB 1358, which requires state agencies to raise rates each year on their recurring contracts with nonprofit human services providers. Starting July 1 2027, the annual increase equals the previous year's rise in the Northeast consumer price index, and an agency may not cut the rate when that index falls. It covers providers serving people with physical, intellectual, or developmental disabilities, and providers of behavioral health services. It passed the Connecticut State Senate 28-8 and became law.

judgments.yea_description: Voted to pass SB 1444, which lets municipalities approve converting commercial buildings into housing through a summary review, with no public hearing and no variance or special permit. The owner must certify that the building was vacant, or averaged under 50% occupancy for the year before applying, and the zoning commission must decide within 65 days. Industrial buildings such as warehouses and factories are not covered. It passed the Connecticut House of Representatives 105-43 and became law.

judgments.yea_description: Voted to pass SB 1542, which bars a police officer from using handcuffs on a child the officer knows is under 14, from the child's first contact with the officer until the child is adjudicated delinquent. Handcuffs are still allowed when needed for public safety, when the child uses or threatens physical force against the officer, or when a court orders restraints under its existing policy. It passed the Connecticut House of Representatives 99-49 and became law.
